problem:
Consider the following parabola:

$$
x=-10{t}^{2},\,y=-5t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

The Cartesian equation of the parabola is

${y}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =-\frac{x}{10},\,t=-\frac{y}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-\frac{x}{10}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{25} & =-\frac{x}{10} \\ {y}^{2} & =-\frac{5}{2}x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${y}^{2}=-\frac{5}{2}x$
